sentences.text: His father was driving the motorbike following all traffic rules and regulations, carefully, in his own lane and at a low speed and was coming from CITI Mall to his home.

5. However, when the applicant reached opposite Meghdoot Apartments, Sector 7, Dwarka near Ramphal Chowk, a car of make Ford Ikon, bearing registration no. DL3CAN0348, was parked in a stationary position on the left side of the road.

6. When the motor bike on which applicant was travelling with his father reached near above said car, Respondent no.1/driver of the Car suddenly, without taking any due precaution or caring for the safety of other commuters on the road, opened the driver's door in full swing and sudden and abrupt opening of the door by Respondent no.1 put the life and safety of applicant and his father in extreme danger.
7.

It is stated that the applicant's father tried hard to stop the motorbike and navigate the same to safety but due to sudden and abrupt opening of the door of the car, he could not manage to avert the impact and ultimately the same resulted in collision of left edge of the handle of the bike with the car and as a result of this both the applicant as well as his father fell down from their motorbike on the road.
8. It is stated that after the accident, father of the applicant got up as he escaped the accident with minor injuries but found petitioner in despairing and unbearable pain.
9. Respondent No. 1 helped father of the claimant in taking claimant in his car to Ayushman Hospital where he left them and drove away from the hospital.
10. It is stated that on preliminary investigation it was diagnosed that applicant has suffered pelvic fracture and urethral injury.
11. On catheterisation, applicant did not void urine and was provided with supra pubic catheter.

12. It is stated that applicant remained on bed without any movement for two weeks with traction on both the legs with weights.
13.

It is stated that the applicant was also admitted in Sir Ganga Ram Hospital on 7.6.2009 to be operated upon on 8.6.2009 but the treating doctor informed that applicant could not be operated upon as gap of strictures was found too big and there was no expectation of a good result by conducting such an operation.
14. It is stated that applicant was given treatment by way of cystoscopy and was discharged thereafter.

15. It is further stated that on 12.6.2009, applicant's parents went to Safdarjang Hospital, New Delhi where HOD Urology Dr. N.K.Mohanty advised for an open surgery (Urethroplasty) operation without any surety of 100% success.

sentences.text: It is his consistent case in claim petition as well as in his evidence by way of affidavit that Respondent No. 1 suddenly, without taking any due precautions or caring for the safety of other commuters on the road, had opened the driver's door in full swing.

59. In Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors. 1999 ACJ 634, the Hon'ble Gawhati High Court has observed as under: "In deciding a matter tribunal should bear in mind the caution struck by the Apex Court that a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal is neither a criminal case nor a civil case.

entities.text: Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors. 1999 ACJ 634
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In a criminal case in order to have conviction, the matter is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt and in a civil case the matter is to be decided on the basis of preponderance of evidence, but in a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal the standard of proof is much below than what is required in a criminal case as well as in a civil case.
No doubt before the tribunal there must be some material on the basis of which the tribunal can arrive or decide things necessary to be decided for awarding compensation.
But the tribunal is not expected to take or to adopt the nicety of a civil or of a criminal case.
After all, it is a summary inquiry and this is a legislation for the welfare of the society"
60 . In the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Vijay Laxmi & Ors.

It was to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."

sentences.text:
On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in F.I.R No. 955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle; (ii)
criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of chargesheet under Sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of F.I.R., wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased.
These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
Proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.
Hence, this contention of the counsel for the appellant also falls face down.
There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on the part of the driver."

62. This case was noticed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case titled as Cholamandalam M.S.
General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Kamlesh: 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310 where adverse inference was drawn because the driver of the offending vehicle had not appeared in the witness box to corroborate his defence taken in the written statement.

ISSUE NO.

In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. ACJ 2011 (Vol. I), following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims:
(i) The compensation payable to the claimant who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. ACJ 2011 (Vol. I)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner.
(ii) Compensation payable in injury   cases
is payable under two heads.
They are  pecuniary damages (special damages) and non pecuniary damages.

Pecuniary damages have three sub heads which are : (i) expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) (a) Loss of earning ( and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising of loss of earning during the period of Rahul Jangid (Aged About 13 Years) vs Prince Lawrence Dhyrianathan on 30 January, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49828600/
7 treatment and (b) loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability (iii) Future medical expenses.

entities.text: Rahul Jangid (Aged About 13 Years) vs Prince Lawrence Dhyrianathan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Nonpecuniary damages (General Damage) are (iv) damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of injuries (v) loss of amenities (and /or loss of prospects of marriage) and (vi) loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

(iii) In routine personal injury cases compensation is awarded only under heads (i),
(ii)(a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation is granted under any of the heads (ii)
(b), (iii) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospectus of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. ACJ 2011 (Vol. I), following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims:
(i) The compensation payable to the claimant who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner.
(ii) Compensation payable in injury   cases
is payable under two heads.
They are  pecuniary damages (special damages) and non pecuniary damages.
Nonpecuniary damages (General Damage) are (iv) damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of injuries (v) loss of amenities (and /or loss of prospects of marriage) and (vi) loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
(iii) In routine personal injury cases compensation is awarded only under heads (i),
(ii)(a) and (iv).
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation is granted under any of the heads (ii)
(b), (iii) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospectus of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
